audience: Hermes Agent users who want a multi-page website prototype from a one-line brief
people who want to watch, steer and edit the build as it happens rather than wait for a finished file
problem: Asking a single chat model for a website means waiting on one long answer and then reading code to see whether it worked. There is nothing to watch, steer or click until it is done.
solution: Swarm Studio splits the site into pages and sections and gives them to a pool of agents that build at the same time on a live canvas, then turns the result into a clickable prototype that can be published or grown into an app.
mechanism: one streamed call plans the theme, shared nav and footer, and the pages
a planner per page breaks it into layers and queues each one as soon as it is ready
a fixed pool of agents takes layers off the queue and streams HTML onto the canvas

evidence.claim: A planner, per-page planners and a pool of agents build the pages in parallel on a canvas.
evidence.supports: The README describes the sitemap call, the page planners, the shared queue and the agent pool.
evidence.limits: It describes the design; it does not measure build time or output quality.

evidence.claim: The canvas server listens on 127.0.0.1 only and the API needs a per-install token.
evidence.source: README.md, What it does on your machine
evidence.supports: The README states the bind address, the Host check and the token stored with mode 0600.
evidence.limits: It is the documented behaviour; the CI check covers the token refusal but not the Host check.

boundaries: Generated sites are prototypes until the App tab builds them into an app.
The canvas runs on the computer's 127.0.0.1, so the Hermes phone webapp cannot reach it.
Builder models must speak the OpenAI chat completions API.
